answer: A graph-based trust protocol resists Sybil attacks by bounding transaction capacity across verified peer-to-peer relationships. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of cultivating genuine, reciprocal interaction history per identity. Bottleneck cuts prevent a plume of fabricated nodes from distorting the network reputation signal, anchoring trust in a decentralized crystal lattice of vouchers. A key limitation is that legitimate newcomers face severe cold-start isolation.
